entities.summary: Zhang Han was a Chinese military general of the Qin dynasty. Born in unknown circumstances, he rose to prominence in the early 3rd century BCE as a skilled commander and strategist. Between 209 and 208 BC, when uprisings against the Qin dynasty broke out, Zhang Han led Qin forces into battle against the various rebel groups and defeated some of them. However, they lost to rebel forces led by Xiang Yu in 207 BC at the Battle of Julu and were forced to surrender. After the rebels overthrew the Qin dynasty in 206 BC, China was divided into the Eighteen Kingdoms and the three surrendered provinces. Zhang Han's legacy as a military leader and statesman endured, but his own fate remained shrouded in mystery. His story serves as a poignant reminder of the complexities and challenges of ancient Chinese history.
